title: 42. Numeracy & Number Systems: Decimal Division
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Decimal Division by a Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Divide a decimal by a one-digit whole number accurately.
questions.question: Calculate \(8.4\div 2\).
questions.explanation: Divide \(8.4\) by \(2\). Since \(84\div 2=42\), placing the decimal point one place from the right gives \(4.2\). Therefore, \(8.4\div 2=4.2\).
questions.hint: Think of \(8.4\) as \(84\) tenths, divide by \(2\), then express the result in decimal form.

questions.concept: Decimal Division by a Decimal Less Than One
questions.learningObjective: Divide a decimal by a one-digit decimal by converting the divisor to a whole number.
questions.question: Calculate \(6.3\div 0.9\).
questions.explanation: Multiply both the dividend and divisor by \(10\): \(6.3\div 0.9=63\div 9\). Since \(63\div 9=7\), the quotient is \(7\).
questions.hint: Multiply both the dividend and divisor by the same power of \(10\) so that the divisor becomes a whole number.

questions.concept: Decimal Division by a Decimal Less Than One
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent division to calculate a decimal quotient.
questions.question: Calculate \(4.8\div 0.6\).
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by \(10\): \(4.8\div 0.6=48\div 6\). Since \(48\div 6=8\), the correct quotient is \(8\).
questions.hint: First make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both numbers by \(10\).

questions.concept: Decimal Division by a Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Divide a decimal with hundredths by a whole number.
questions.question: Calculate \(7.56\div 3\).
questions.hint: Keep track of place value as you divide the ones, tenths, and hundredths.

questions.concept: Effect of Dividing by a Decimal Less Than One
questions.learningObjective: Calculate and interpret a quotient when the divisor is less than one.
questions.question: Which statement is correct about \(12.5\div 0.5\)?

options.label: A
options.text: The quotient is \(2.5\), so it is smaller than \(12.5\).

options.label: B
options.text: The quotient is \(25\), so it is larger than \(12.5\).

questions.explanation: Dividing by \(0.5\) asks how many halves are contained in \(12.5\). Since \(12.5\div 0.5=125\div 5=25\), the quotient is \(25\), which is larger than \(12.5\).
questions.hint: Rewrite the division so the divisor is a whole number, then compare the quotient with the dividend.

questions.learningObjective: Divide decimals by converting a two-digit decimal divisor to a whole number.
questions.question: Calculate \(3.24\div 0.12\).
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by \(100\): \(3.24\div 0.12=324\div 12\). Since \(324\div 12=27\), the quotient is \(27\).
questions.hint: Multiply both numbers by a power of \(10\) that makes \(0.12\) a whole number.

questions.learningObjective: Use decimal division to determine an unknown factor.
questions.question: A number multiplied by \(0.7\) equals \(5.04\). What is the number?
questions.explanation: If the unknown number is \(x\), then \(0.7x=5.04\). Divide both sides by \(0.7\): \(x=5.04\div 0.7=50.4\div 7=7.2\). Therefore, the number is \(7.2\).
questions.hint: Undo multiplication by \(0.7\) using division, then make the divisor a whole number.

questions.learningObjective: Divide by a decimal in hundredths using equivalent division.
questions.question: Calculate \(18.9\div 0.09\).
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by \(100\): \(18.9\div 0.09=1890\div 9\). Since \(1890\div 9=210\), the quotient is \(210\).
questions.hint: Make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both the dividend and divisor by \(100\).

questions.learningObjective: Verify a decimal quotient using multiplication.
questions.question: A learner claims that \(6.72\div 1.6=4.2\). Which calculation correctly verifies the claim?
questions.explanation: Division can be checked by multiplying the quotient by the divisor. Here, \(42\times 16=672\), and the factors have \(1+1=2\) decimal places in total, so \(4.2\times 1.6=6.72\), which reproduces the dividend. The other calculation uses \(0.16\), which is not the divisor (and \(4.2\times 0.16=0.672\), not \(6.72\)). Therefore, the claim \(6.72\div 1.6=4.2\) is verified.
questions.hint: To check a division result, multiply the proposed quotient by the original divisor and compare the product with the dividend.

questions.concept: Decimal Division in a Rate Context
questions.learningObjective: Apply decimal division to determine time from a total amount and a constant decimal rate.
questions.question: A machine fills containers at a constant rate of \(2.5\) liters per minute. How many minutes are needed to fill \(15.75\) liters?
questions.explanation: Time equals total amount divided by the rate: \(15.75\div 2.5\). Multiply both numbers by \(10\): \(157.5\div 25=6.3\). Therefore, the machine needs \(6.3\) minutes.
questions.hint: Use \(\text{time}=\text{total amount}\div\text{rate}\), then make the divisor a whole number.
